steps.content: They drive their blades into Hilda's chest, opening a wound.
She does not struggle, allowing the ghosts to lift her heart from its cradle.
In that moment, even the ghosts fall silent. Their angry shrieks and agonized wails die away. They simply stare, as you do, transfixed.
It is a heart of neither pure white nor wicked black—but mottled gray, caught in the eternal struggle between right and wrong, light and darkness.
It is a landscape of cracks, as though torn apart countless times, each fissure overlaid with the scar tissue of its own desperate repairs.
It is neither pure nor perfect—a thing shattered and remade, as full of weakness as it is of scars.
It is, ultimately, not what anyone has hoped to see.
When you look back at Hilda, her eyes are closed, as if she has finally, after a long and weary battle, found her peace.
